chunks: Then you were taken out from your place of stay to a place you had not seen,
and who guided you to eke out your sustenance from the udder of your mother, and, when you were in need, appraised you of the location of what you required or aimed at?!

Alas! Certainly he who is unable to understand the qualities of a being with shape and limbs is the more unable to understand the qualities of the Creator and the more remote from appreciating Him through the limitations of creatures.
ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha argue for the knowability of God's attributes through human experience?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this passage as a cornerstone of Shia theological epistemology, arguing that the innate, untaught knowledge of created attributes (like nursing) serves as a valid analogical basis for knowing the Creator, thereby refuting extreme anthropomorphism and agnosticism. This reasoning underscores the Shia belief in the accessibility of divine knowledge through the observation of creation, linking the microcosm of human experience to the macrocosm of God's attributes.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Then you were taken out from your place of stay to a place you had not seen, and you were not acquainted with the means of awaiting its benefits,
or with who guided you to eke out your sustenance from the udder of your mother, and, when you were in need, appraised you of the location of what you required or aimed at.

Alas ! Certainly he who is unable to understand the qualities of a being with shape and limbs is the more unable to understand the qualities of the Creator and the more remote from appreciating Him through the limitations of creatures.
